html:
The Crown of Castile was the largest kingdom of medieval Spain, formed in 1230 when Ferdinand III joined Castile and León for good. On the map for 1279 to 1400 it covers most of the peninsula, from Galicia to Andalusia, leaving Portugal, Aragon, Navarre and Granada around it.

Ferdinand III took Córdoba in 1236 and Seville in 1248, leaving only Granada in Muslim hands. His son Alfonso X, the Wise, had laws, histories and science written in Castilian instead of Latin, including the law code of the Siete Partidas, and backed translators in Toledo. The wool of Castile's merino sheep, moved each year by the herders' guild, the Mesta, was sold to Flanders.

A civil war in the 1360s brought the Trastámara family to the throne. Its heiress Isabella married Ferdinand of Aragon in 1469. Under them Castile backed Columbus's voyage of 1492, so the Americas became Castilian lands. Castile was the core of Spain.
